notice: The single authoritative run-lifecycle and safety contract. The recorder changes state only through this table and seals completion through the finalization protocol below; the verifier loads the same file, never imports the recorder, never takes a claimed status as truth, and reconstructs every state, counter and stop from the persisted files. Prose: docs/v13j/SAFETY_CONTRACT.md.

acceptance.principle: NEVER FALSELY COMPLETE. The completion seal is the sole authority that a run reached a terminal state; it is necessary, never sufficient. No archive is classified COMPLETE or PARTIAL from the absence of any file or marker.
COMPLETE: a valid completion seal (seal.validity) whose terminalState is COMPLETE
every seal hash equals the bytes on disk
every scheduled draw recorded as a completed ledger row, in schedule order
every required model call accounted: each dispatch intent in the call journal has exactly one outcome and equals the call recorded in its draw
every required health check present exactly once, internally valid, HEALTHY, with an unchanged server signature
no stop, no failure event, no aborted draw, no interrupted row, no unresolved dispatch
cleanup SUCCEEDED and recorded as specified
every required artifact present and finalized; every forbidden artifact absent (not JSON null)
operator interrupts, if any, only with disposition AFTER_SCHEDULE
independent model-free replay of every completed row passes (analysis)
PARTIAL: a valid completion seal whose terminalState is PARTIAL
every seal hash equals the bytes on disk
a truthful stop record: exactly one admissible stop (or a cleanup-created stop) whose code, state, fields and evidence satisfy stopCodes and the per-stage evidence table
a valid completed-draw prefix: ledger rows are schedule[0:n], each completed row complete and replayable, at most the last interrupted by a guard halt
no contradictory evidence: every structural, transition, accounting, health, cleanup, interrupt and timestamp rule holds exactly as for COMPLETE
every event that cannot be independently reconstructed carries an explicit verificationStatus (UNVERIFIED) and never excuses a structural contradiction
no complete-run arm comparison or pair summary is produced
acceptance.INVALID: any archive that is unsealed, malformed, incomplete, contradictory, unsupported or unverifiable beyond the PARTIAL contract; INVALID is assigned only by the verifier and analysis refuses it

severity.meaning: an incomplete, contradictory or insufficiently durable archive classified COMPLETE
a contradictory archive accepted because its status is PARTIAL or its cause is UNVERIFIED
a genuine failure the recorder could have finalized is safely rejected; no evidence misrepresented; nothing resumed

severity.class: lost completed draw or known model call
severity.meaning: a completed draw or a dispatched model call missing from the persisted evidence, even of a rejected run

CREATED.meaning: archive directory, empty ledger, empty call journal and initial manifest persisted

PREFLIGHT.meaning: limits configured; the initial health read, when the server is observed, is in progress

HEALTH_CHECK.meaning: the round-boundary health read before the next draw is in progress

DRAW_ACTIVE.meaning: the draw guard passed for schedule[committed]; the draw is executing, or returned and not yet committed

DRAW_RECORDED.meaning: the draw's row is durable in the ledger and bound by a commit_draw journal entry

CLEANUP.meaning: no further draw starts; pooled engine sessions are being released

FINALIZING.meaning: cleanup recorded in the final manifest; side artifacts and the completion seal are being written; the archive is unsealed

COMPLETE.meaning: terminal; exists only as the transition recorded in a valid completion seal

PARTIAL.meaning: terminal; exists only as the transition recorded in a valid completion seal

INVALID.meaning: assigned by the verifier to any archive that is unsealed or violates an invariant; never written by the recorder

events.begin_preflight: limits configured next; the initial health read follows when the server is observed
events.preflight_passed: initial observation HEALTHY (or the server is not observed in a checked fixture)
events.health_passed: round-boundary observation HEALTHY and the server signature unchanged
events.commit_draw: the active draw's row is durable in draws.json
events.continue: the committed row completed and draws remain
events.schedule_done: the committed row completed and it was the last scheduled draw
events.cleanup_succeeded: pooled session release returned normally; recorded in the final manifest
events.cleanup_failed: pooled session release raised; recorded in the final manifest separately from any primary stop
events.finalize_complete: the completion seal (terminalState COMPLETE) was renamed into place; recorded only in the seal
events.finalize_partial: the completion seal (terminalState PARTIAL) was renamed into place; recorded only in the seal

transitionPredicates.create: first journal entry; run.started equals its timestamp
transitionPredicates.preflight_passed: server observed: the PREFLIGHT visit made exactly one health check whose kept observation is HEALTHY; server not observed (checked fixture only): no health check
transitionPredicates.begin_health_check: the server is observed, committed < drawsScheduled, the schedule requires a round check before schedule[committed] (committed == 0 or (model, draw) differs from schedule[committed-1]), and no earlier visit served schedule[committed]
transitionPredicates.health_passed: the visit's single check kept a HEALTHY observation and its server signature equals the initial signature; healthCheck names that check
transitionPredicates.begin_draw: draw == schedule[committed].seq; the preceding entry is health_passed for this draw when a round check is required, otherwise preflight_passed (committed == 0) or continue
transitionPredicates.commit_draw: follows the begin_draw of the same draw; draw, status, rowSha256 and modelCalls equal ledger row committed+1; reconciled true only when the next entry is stop
transitionPredicates.continue: the committed row is completed and committed < drawsScheduled
transitionPredicates.schedule_done: the committed row is completed and committed == drawsScheduled
transitionPredicates.stop: at most one; code admissible in its from-state with the evidence stopCodes requires
transitionPredicates.cleanup_succeeded: cleanup.status SUCCEEDED, failure null, timestamp equal to the entry
transitionPredicates.cleanup_failed: cleanup.status FAILED with failure {type, message}, timestamp equal to the entry; without an earlier stop the manifest carries a driver stop at CLEANUP equal to that failure
transitionPredicates.finalize_complete: only in the seal; the derived state is COMPLETE
transitionPredicates.finalize_partial: only in the seal; the derived state is PARTIAL

illegalTransitions: every (from, event) pair not listed, any transition out of a terminal state, any transition into INVALID, a seal-only event in the manifest journal, any unsatisfied transition predicate, and any unknown state or event name: the recorder refuses it; the verifier classifies the archive INVALID

safePoints.note: SIGINT is handled by a minimal handler that only counts the signal; it never raises. A pending interrupt is examined only at these declared points. STOP points may record an operator stop; NOTE points never act (they lie inside evidence-transfer windows) and leave the interrupt pending for the next STOP point; RECORD points (after the run stopped or the schedule completed) record the interrupt without changing the outcome.

before_dispatch.where: the draw guard's before-request check, before the dispatch intent is written; nothing of the request exists yet
before_dispatch.stop: the draw is aborted at failureStage workflow with failure {type OperatorStop}; calls already recorded are kept

after_transport_returns.where: the transport returned; its result has not yet reached the call journal or the draw's evidence

after_call_persisted.where: the call outcome is durable in the call journal; the draw's in-memory evidence is about to record it

after_draw_persisted.where: commit_draw is durable and the committed row is completed

between_draws.where: before the next draw's round health check and draw guard

before_health_check.where: before a health read starts; no check is appended
before_health_check.stop: operator stop from that state without a health check

after_health_check.where: the read returned and its observation is HEALTHY with an unchanged signature (a health or server_change stop takes precedence)
after_health_check.stop: operator stop from that state, the check kept

before_cleanup.where: before the pooled session release, which always runs

after_cleanup.where: after the release returned or raised

before_finalization.where: immediately before the final manifest (cleanup transition) is written; the last point whose interrupts reach the archive

dispositions.STOP: the interrupt became the run's operator stop at that STOP point
dispositions.AFTER_STOP: observed after another stop was recorded; the primary stop is unchanged
dispositions.AFTER_SCHEDULE: observed after schedule_done with no stop; a post-completion operator event, admissible in COMPLETE

safePoints.unarchived: an interrupt received after before_finalization is reported only through the public run result (interrupts.unarchived); it cannot alter an archive whose content is already fixed
safePoints.windows: between a durable dispatch intent and the transport call, and between the transport's return and the draw's own evidence append, no recorder exception propagates: a recorder fault there is deferred to the next STOP point as a driver stop, and a persistence fault poisons the archive (it is never sealed)
safePoints.engineIsolation: engine subprocesses run in their own session (process group) so that a terminal SIGINT reaches only the recorder; the engine and its requests are unchanged

health.requires: the visit's check kept a non-HEALTHY observation

server_change.requires: HEALTHY round observation whose server signature differs from the initial signature

wall_clock.requires: READY: draw-guard halt (stage draw_start, drawCalls 0); DRAW_RECORDED: equal to the committed interrupted row's halt

draw_call_limit.requires: equal to the committed interrupted row's halt (stage request_start)

call_budget.requires: equal to the committed interrupted row's halt (stage request_start)

transport.requires: equal to the committed interrupted row's halt (stage request_start)

fields.healthCheck: after_health_check: the visit's check; otherwise null
fields.safePoint: a STOP safe point admissible in the stop's state

operator.requires: exactly one interrupt event with disposition STOP at the same safe point, state and timestamp; DRAW_ACTIVE: the aborted artifact has failureStage workflow, failure type OperatorStop and stopReason operator; DRAW_RECORDED: the committed row is completed

fields.request: the health request iff a read was attempted in this visit and neither kept nor rejected an observation

driver.requires: DRAW_ACTIVE: the aborted artifact's failure equals stop.failure; DRAW_RECORDED: the committed row is completed; a rejected observation stops the run as driver; CLEANUP only as a cleanup-created stop through cleanup_failed with no earlier stop

abortedDraw.note: An aborted draw is the next scheduled draw, never a ledger row, persisted only for a stop from DRAW_ACTIVE. Each failureStage fixes every evidence field exactly; the verifier checks each field, recomputes process evidence from the artifact's own engine log and calls, and never accepts UNVERIFIED as an excuse.

fieldValues.recordedCalls: the recorded calls, equal one-to-one to this draw's resolved call-journal entries
fieldValues.derivedProcess: the process evidence recomputed from the artifact's engine log, calls and pending message

draw_setup.meaning: an exception before the draw runner was entered

draw_unrecorded.meaning: the draw runner was entered and raised without its own evidence; the call journal is the only call evidence
draw_unrecorded.journalCalls: any, all resolved; counted in modelCalls; never reported as zero

workflow.reconstruction: transport replay when the last call raised (no body); boundary replay when stopped at before_dispatch; otherwise UNVERIFIED

fields.halt: null, or a halt (then record null)
fields.record: null, or an object (then halt null)

fields.halt: null, or a halt (then record null)
fields.record: null, or an object (then halt null)

abortedDraw.common: status aborted; verificationStatus UNVERIFIED; failure {type, message}; stopReason equal to the stop code; failure type OperatorStop iff stop code operator (and then failureStage workflow); identity equal to schedule[committed]

callJournal.encoding: one canonical JSON object per line (sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII), each appended and fsynced before the operation it records continues

dispatch.meaning: written in the draw guard's before-request check after the stop and limit checks pass, immediately before the request is handed to the transport: the request may have been sent from this moment

returned.meaning: the transport returned (status, body, error); body is the response text or null

raised.meaning: the transport raised; the request's server-side outcome is unknown (UNRESOLVED); exception {type, message}

rules: k counts dispatches in the run from 1; n counts dispatches in the draw from 1
records alternate dispatch(k), outcome(k) in k order; a dispatch without an outcome is an unresolved call and makes a sealed archive INVALID (an unsealed archive keeps it as evidence)
each draw's resolved entries equal its recorded calls one-to-one: n, requestSha256; returned: status, error, responseSha256 and body; raised: status null, body null, error 'client: {type}: {message}'
only draws begun in the journal appear; a draw with no entries has no recorded calls
modelCalls counts dispatches; it is never derived from an artifact whose calls are unknown

health.bodyRule: bytes over maxBodyBytes: oversized_body; not strict UTF-8: non_utf8_body; not JSON: invalid_json; not an object: not_an_object; an object with a key named error and status "healthy": contradictory_body; status not a non-empty string: missing_status; status "healthy": healthy; any other status: unhealthy_status. A body category requires a 2xx HTTP status, no exception and a valid stored body.
health.exceptionEvidence: {type, reasonType, reasonKind}: type is the exception's exact class as module.qualname; for urllib.error.URLError reasonKind is exception (reasonType the reason's exact class) or text (reasonType null); otherwise reasonType and reasonKind are null
health.readFailureRule: the recorder normalizes the exception object by its exact class (never a superclass, never message text): an unwrapped exception whose exact class is listed takes that family; urllib.error.URLError with an exception reason whose exact class is listed in a wrappable family takes that family; URLError with a text reason is url_error; HTTPError is http_status. Any other exception, including KeyboardInterrupt, ValueError, an unlisted OSError subclass or a URLError with an unlisted reason, is not a health read failure: it propagates and stops the run as a driver failure with the attempted request recorded and no observation. Every read failure has outcome READ_FAILED, no parsed body (http_status may retain the error body) and cause UNVERIFIED.
health.verifierRule: the verifier never trusts a recorded type name: it requires type and reasonType to be listed exactly in the family named by category, with the reasonKind the rule implies, and re-classifies every body from its stored bytes
health.contradiction: an observation whose category, outcome, HTTP status, exception, body, hash or timestamps disagree is invalid evidence; the recorder refuses it before it can justify continuing (driver stop, the value kept as rejected) and the verifier re-checks independently; it is never HEALTHY
health.noInvention: a read that raised an unclassified exception records the attempted request and no observation; no response is substituted

healthSchedule: ordinary runs observe the server; only an explicitly checked record-only fixture may leave it unobserved. When observed: one PREFLIGHT visit with exactly one read, then exactly one HEALTH_CHECK visit, with exactly one read, before schedule[i] whenever i == 0 or (model, draw) differs from schedule[i-1]; no other visit and no second visit for the same draw

artifacts.run.json: manifest: identities, claimed non-terminal state, journal (never a seal-only event), counters, health checks, stop, failure event, cleanup, interrupts
artifacts.draws.json: authoritative ledger of committed draw/v4 rows; atomic replacement at each commit
artifacts.calls.jsonl: durable call journal; append and fsync per record
artifacts.server-before.json: the initial server state; present iff the initial read kept an observation
artifacts.aborted-draw.json: present iff the stop is from DRAW_ACTIVE
artifacts.failure-event.json: present iff a stop exists; equal to run.failureEvent
artifacts.SEAL.json: the completion seal; written last; its presence alone never establishes acceptance

absence: a side artifact that the derived state forbids must be absent; a present file containing JSON null, or any value of the wrong type, is a contradiction, never absence

counters.drawInterrupted: seq of the interrupted ledger row, or null
counters.drawAborted: seq of the aborted artifact, or null
counters.modelCalls: dispatch records in the call journal
counters.healthChecks: recorded health checks, interrupted and rejected reads included

interrupts.record: run.interrupts = {signal: SIGINT, events: [{n, safePoint, state, signals, disposition, timestamp}]}
rules: events are in n order with non-decreasing timestamps; signals >= 1
an operator stop exists iff exactly one event has disposition STOP, and it names the stop's safe point and state with the stop transition's timestamp
AFTER_STOP events only after a stop, from a RECORD safe point in CLEANUP
AFTER_SCHEDULE events only after schedule_done with no stop, from a RECORD safe point in CLEANUP
interrupts.publicResult: run_schedule returns {state, runId, archive, manifest, seal, interrupts {signalsReceived, archived, unarchived, stopSafePoint, postCompletion}, commit {sealRenamed, directorySync, postCommitError}}; a RecordingError carries the same interrupts summary; no interrupt is silently discarded

timestamps.grammar: UTC RFC 3339 profile, matched against the whole string: [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]{1,6})?Z with ASCII digits only, no surrounding or trailing characters (a trailing newline is rejected), and a valid calendar date and time
timestamps.order: run.started equals the create entry; journal timestamps non-decreasing; the seal transition timestamp >= the last journal entry; each kept observation started <= ended inside its visit; failureEvent.timestamp equals the stop transition (or the cleanup_failed entry for a cleanup-created stop); cleanup.timestamp equals its transition; each draw's call sent times and call-journal times non-decreasing inside its begin_draw..commit/stop interval, with sent <= dispatch <= outcome for each call; interrupt events inside the run
timestamps.provenance: run.provenance.timestamps SYSTEM_UTC for ordinary runs; SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE only for reproducible record-only fixtures, refused unless the verifier is explicitly asked to check a fixture
timestamps.replay: timestamps are metadata; deterministic draw replay identities exclude them; a missing timestamp is never inferred

steps: cleanup: release pooled engine sessions (always attempted); safe points before_cleanup, after_cleanup, before_finalization record pending interrupts
write run.json with the cleanup transition (state FINALIZING): file write, flush, file fsync, same-directory atomic replace, directory fsync
write failure-event.json when a stop exists, the same way
refuse to seal if any persistence operation of the run failed (the archive is poisoned)
re-read every archive file from disk and compute the seal's hashes from those bytes
write the seal to a temporary file in the archive directory: write, flush, file fsync
rename the temporary file to SEAL.json (os.replace): THE COMMIT POINT and the last required operation
after the commit point, best effort only: directory fsync; its result is reported (commit.directorySync) and never changes the archive or its classification
finalization.commitPoint: the atomic rename of the fully written and fsynced seal into SEAL.json; before it the archive is unsealed and INVALID; after it nothing required remains
finalization.failure: any failure or process termination before the commit point leaves no SEAL.json (the temporary file is removed when possible; a stray temporary file is itself INVALID); no marker restoration or recovery write is ever needed

durability.processCrash: CLAIMED: under termination of the recording process at any instant (SIGKILL included), the archive is either unsealed (INVALID) or sealed with every byte the seal binds already written; rename atomicity within one directory makes the seal appear all at once. Tested by real SIGKILL at every reached operation boundary.
durability.powerLoss: NOT CLAIMED. Design intent only: every bound file and its directory entry is fsynced before the seal is written, and the seal is fsynced before its rename, so on a filesystem that honours fsync ordering a seal that survives power loss binds durable content, and a lost rename reverts to an unsealed (INVALID) archive. The post-rename directory fsync is best effort; if it fails or is lost the completion may revert to INVALID after power loss, never to a false COMPLETE. Hardware or filesystems that acknowledge fsync without persisting can defeat this; no test covers power loss.
durability.multiFile: there is no multi-file transaction; consistency comes from the single commit point and the verifier's hash and semantic checks

seal.validity: exact field set; schema, finalization contract, lifecycle id and SHA-256, run schema, driver, runId, protocol {id, sha256} and schedule SHA-256 equal the manifest and the verifier's inputs; transition {n, event, from FINALIZING, to, timestamp} with event finalize_complete iff to COMPLETE and n = journal length + 1; manifest {file, sha256, journalEntries}; ledger {file, sha256, rows, completed, rowSha256[]}; calls {file, sha256, records, dispatched}; health {checks, checkSha256[], serverBefore}; sideArtifacts {server-before.json, aborted-draw.json, failure-event.json}: SHA-256 or null; counters equal to the manifest. A null hash requires the file to be absent.
seal.authority: a missing seal means not terminal (INVALID); a malformed, mismatching or contradictory seal means INVALID; a valid seal is necessary, never sufficient: every semantic rule is verified independently and the derived terminal state must equal terminalState

kinds.exception: RuntimeError raised at the point (a recorder fault)
kinds.signal: a real SIGINT delivered to the recording process at the point (os.kill of its own pid); the handler only counts it
kinds.persistence: OSError(EIO) from the filesystem operation at the point
kinds.persistent: every filesystem write, sync, replace, rename and unlink in the archive directory fails with OSError(EIO) from the point on, including any operation attempted after the first failure
kinds.transport: a genuine transport failure: health read -> connection refused through the production probe; model call -> failed exchange without a response
kinds.guard_halt: the run clock passes the wall-clock stop at the draw guard
kinds.kill: SIGKILL of the recording process at the point (real subprocess harness only)

persist:calls_init.context: the empty call journal, before the manifest exists

persist:manifest.context: every transition checkpoint, identified by its event

append:calls.context: a dispatch intent or a call outcome

expected.NO_ARCHIVE: a fault before the initial manifest is durable: recording failure; no seal; INVALID
expected.FAIL_CLOSED: a persistence fault, a persistent filesystem failure before the commit point, or a recorder fault inside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence other than the session release: recording failure; no seal; INVALID
expected.COMMITTED: any fault at or after seal.renamed: the seal is in place; the run result is returned with the fault reported (commit.directorySync / postCommitError); the archive is classified by its content (COMPLETE or PARTIAL as the base)
expected.HANDLED: a recorder fault outside persistence and outside the stop sequence: stop driver at the state current at the fault (after reconciling the committed ledger); PARTIAL; inside a transport window the fault is deferred to the next STOP point
expected.INTERRUPT: a real SIGINT: the first safe point at or after the injection decides: a STOP point while running -> operator stop at that point (PARTIAL); a RECORD point after a stop -> AFTER_STOP (outcome unchanged); after schedule_done -> AFTER_SCHEDULE (COMPLETE unchanged); after before_finalization -> unarchived, reported in the result
expected.HEALTH_STOP: transport fault during a health read: stop health with a READ_FAILED observation; PARTIAL
expected.GUARD_STOP: guard_halt: stop wall_clock at READY; PARTIAL
expected.CLEANUP_FAILED: a recorder fault during the session release: cleanup FAILED; an earlier stop stays primary, otherwise stop driver at CLEANUP; PARTIAL
expected.WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE: model transport failure: a recorded failed exchange inside the draw; the base outcome with one more call
expected.KILLED: SIGKILL: before the commit point no seal (INVALID) with every durable row and journal entry kept; at or after seal.renamed the archive is sealed and classified by its content

expectedRule.when: kind persistence or persistent, a persist/append/seal phase other than before/after, or seal.before
append:calls after phase of a dispatch intent, before/after phase of an outcome record, or a NOTE safe point (inside a transport window)
expectedRule.expect: HANDLED (deferred to the next STOP point)

expectedRule.when: inside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence and not session_cleanup.during

S01.name: seal present
S01.rule: an archive without SEAL.json is unsealed and INVALID whatever its manifest claims

S02.name: seal identity
S02.rule: finalization.seal.validity: schema, contract versions and every identity equal the manifest and the verifier's inputs

S03.name: seal hashes
S03.rule: every seal hash equals the bytes on disk; a null hash requires absence; per-row and per-check hashes equal the canonical JSON of the ledger rows and health checks

S04.name: seal terminal state
S04.rule: the seal transition is FINALIZING -> terminalState with the matching event and n, timestamped no earlier than the journal; terminalState equals the state the evidence supports

L01.name: schedule prefix
L01.rule: ledger rows are schedule[0:n] in order with exact identities, each once; only the last may be interrupted; an aborted draw is schedule[n]

L02.name: completed evidence
L02.rule: every completed row has the complete draw/v4 evidence: record, batches, exact submitted representation and hash, process, initial and final digests, engine log, calls, READY initialization, RECORDED, no failure, cleanupFailure or stopReason

L03.name: draw conservation
L03.rule: drawsScheduled = drawsCompleted + [drawInterrupted] + [drawAborted] + drawsNotRun, each counter equal to the value derived from the artifacts

L04.name: call accounting
L04.rule: callJournal.rules; run, failure-event and halt call counts equal the journal; per-call order, request and response hashes and metadata hold; per-draw and run totals within the protocol bounds; no unknown count reported as zero

L05.name: aborted is not completed
L05.rule: an aborted draw is never a ledger row, only the next scheduled draw, only after a stop from DRAW_ACTIVE

L06.name: per-stage evidence
L06.rule: abortedDraw.stages fixes every field of the aborted artifact for its failureStage; stopCodes fixes every stop field for its code and state

L07.name: health evidence
L07.rule: health checks occur exactly as healthSchedule requires, each visit once; every kept observation is internally consistent, re-classifies from its body or listed exception family, and passing transitions require HEALTHY with an unchanged signature; a rejected observation is invalid and stops the run as driver; server-before.json equals the initial kept observation's state

L08.name: cleanup distinguishable
L08.rule: cleanup SUCCEEDED or FAILED with a separate failure, equal to its transition; a cleanup failure never replaces an earlier stop; a cleanup-created stop equals the cleanup failure

L09.name: no unresolved failure in COMPLETE
L09.rule: COMPLETE has no stop, failure event, aborted artifact, interrupted row, failed cleanup, unresolved dispatch, non-HEALTHY or rejected observation, or interrupt event other than AFTER_SCHEDULE

L10.name: COMPLETE coverage
L10.rule: COMPLETE requires every scheduled draw completed and the journal tail schedule_done, cleanup_succeeded, then the seal's finalize_complete

L11.name: PARTIAL suppression
L11.rule: a PARTIAL analysis has no complete-run arm differences or pair summaries

L12.name: INVALID never passes
L12.rule: any violation classifies the archive INVALID and analysis refuses it

L13.name: timestamps
L13.rule: every required timestamp matches timestamps.grammar exactly and is ordered as timestamps.order requires; synthetic provenance only for explicit fixtures

L14.name: transitions and predicates
L14.rule: the journal starts with create, chains from/to exactly, uses only listed transitions and names, satisfies every transition predicate, holds no seal-only event and ends in FINALIZING

L15.name: identity binding
L15.rule: run schema, driver, lifecycle identity and SHA-256, UUID run identity, protocol identity and hash, and schedule hash agree

L16.name: artifact set
L16.rule: exactly the artifacts the derived state requires, of the right JSON type; no stray or temporary file; no JSON-null side artifact; failure-event.json equal to run.failureEvent

L17.name: journal-ledger binding
L17.rule: begin_draw and commit_draw name the scheduled draws in order; each commit_draw carries the row's canonical SHA-256, status and call count; a reconciled commit is followed by the stop

L18.name: no resume
L18.rule: resume is never; an existing run directory is never reused

L19.name: single consistent stop
L19.rule: at most one stop; run.stop, failureEvent.stop and the journal agree on code and state

L20.name: interrupt evidence
L20.rule: interrupts.rules hold; the operator stop and the STOP event agree; no interrupt event is invented or dropped from the archived record
